newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse cable purchase seen as a plus.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse cable purchase seen as a plus.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's purchase of two popular country music cable networks from Gaylord Entertainment Co will add strong cash flow to its bottom line and give it leverage to expand in sports programming, analysts said Monday.

"I think it's a terrific acquisition," said Ed Hatch at UBS Securities. "It gives Westinghouse added entertainment distribution and increses their ability to buy more sports programming. If they want to make a bid for the NFL (National Football League), they have another distribution channel through which to do that."
Hatch said the acquisition will give Westinghouse about $108 million in cash flow. "I anticipate the networks to have a growth rate of about 18 percent," he added.

Westinghouse said it reached a definitive agreement to acquire Gaylord's two major cable networks -- The Nashville Network (TNN) and Country Music Television (CMT) -- for $1.55 billion in stock. Analysts said they saw no negative impact on Westinghouse from the stock transaction.
TNN broadcasts include popular sports events including NASCAR stock car racing.

Jack Bergen, Westinghouse's senior vice president of corporate relations, said the company hopes to close the transaction early in the third quarter, prior to Westinghouse splitting its industrial and media operations into separate companies.
He said the acquisition would not saddle Westinghouse with any debt and would be accretive to earnings. The deal also would include about $50 million of working capital.

"We had three objectives when we bought CBS," he said. "To turn CBS around, to be the preeminent radio broadcaster and to have a solid position in cable. We've done the first, we've worked on the second and we're in the game now with the third."

Analysts said Westinghouse paid a fair price for the networks. "We did an asset valuation on them recently, and (the purchase price) is roughly what we estimated the value of those businesses at," said Mary Kukowski at Dillon Read. "I think they're strong, attractive businesses and the price is fair."

Kukowski said the acquisition would let Gaylord focus on growing its presence in the hotel and convention business. The company already owns, among other things, the Grand Ole Opry and the Opryland Hotel and convention center in Nashville.

"Gaylord felt the networks' interests were best served in a media company," she said, adding she expected the networks to continue posting above-average cash flow after their sale to Westinghouse. TNN posted '96 revenues of $290 million, while CMT posted revenues last year of $45 million. Total earnings for networks before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization were $105 million.
TNN is the second largest North American network and the eighth largest in the United States, currently reaching more than 70 million households. CMT has nearly 38 million U.S. subscribers.
Westinghouse has been in a partnership with Gaylord since 1982, providing advertising sales and marketing for the two networks through its Group W operations.
"We knew those businesses so well. This was a safe acquisition for us," said Bergen.
Shares of Westinghouse were down 1/4 to 17-1/2 while Gaylord shares fell 2-1/2 to 22-7/8, both in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Included in the merger are CMT Canada, a joint venture with Shaw Cable of Canada, several cable production companies, and NASCAR Thunder, a chain of retail stores themed on NASCAR racing.
